summary:
The main event this week was the site assistant going fully live on phillipsben.com. Six phases end-to-end with Claude: a build-time knowledge pack (~12k tokens of site content) with a redaction guard that makes confidential leaks structurally impossible, a `/ask` API route with a pluggable LLM backend and per-IP rate limiting, a streaming chat overlay with focus-trap and mobile layout, a hero band with chip shortcuts, adversarial hardening, and a flagship write-up. The battery ran 16/16 with zero leaks — fabrication, off-topic, prompt-injection, and open-relay attempts all handled cleanly.

The backend decision was deliberate: the local Tesla P100 path exists and is wired (via Switchboard), but warm prefill latency on the P100 with the full context pack sits around 10s, cold around 48s. Claude Haiku was chosen as the default for responsiveness, with the local option kept as an opt-in.

This week shifted to post-launch cleanup — hero images generated and plumbed for all project pages via a pipeline that runs at build time, plus an invariant guard that fails the build if a project is missing art. The Switchboard-side Modelfile changes from the site-assistant work (new model entry, priority-aware lock) are staged but not yet committed in that repo.

highlights.oneLiner: Site assistant shipped end-to-end — knowledge pack, streaming chat overlay, adversarial hardening (16/16), and flagship write-up all live.
Hero image pipeline landed: generated art for all project pages, build-time invariant guard, and heroes:check helper added.
Daily dashboard cron running stably; pop-os memory snapshot syncing fresh each morning.
